questions.name: Statement: “Book tickets online to avoid the queue at the counter.” — railway notice. Assumptions: I. Passengers generally prefer to avoid queues. II. An online booking facility is available. Which is implicit?
questions.nameText:

 avoid the queue at the counter.” — railway notice.
 Assumptions: I. Passengers generally prefer to avoid queues. II.
 An online booking facility is available. Which is implicit?

options.name: Both I and II are implicit
options.nameText: Both I and II are implicit

questions.solution: The advice is useful only if people want to skip queues (I) and only if online booking actually exists (II). Both assumptions are implicit.

questions.name: If in a certain code, PAPER is written as 16-1-16-5-18 (letter positions in the alphabet), how is PENCIL written using the same rule?
questions.nameText:

 16-1-16-5-18 (letter positions in the alphabet), how is PENCIL
 written using the same rule?
questions.solution: Use each letter’s serial number: P=16, E=5, N=14, C=3, I=9, L=12. So PENCIL → 16-5-14-3-9-12.

questions.name: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 24, 51, 106, ?
questions.nameText:
Find the next number in the series: 5, 11,
 24, 51, 106, ?
questions.solution: Each term is formed as (previous × 2) plus an increasing integer: 5×2+1 = 11, 11×2+2 = 24, 24×2+3 = 51, 51×2+4 = 106. The next term is 106×2+5 = 217.

questions.name: At what time between 4 and 5 o’clock are the hands of a clock at right angles for the later of the two occasions?
questions.nameText:
At what time between 4 and 5 o’clock
 are the hands of a clock at right angles for the later of the two
 occasions?
questions.solution: Use |30H − 5.5M| = 90 with H = 4. This gives 5.5M = 30 or 5.5M = 210, so M = 5 5/11 or M = 38 2/11. The later occasion is 4:38 2/11 minutes.

questions.name: If 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday, what day of the week was 15 August 2024?
questions.nameText:
If 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday, what day of
 the week was 15 August 2024?
questions.solution: 2024 is a leap year and 29 February 2024 falls between the two dates, so the gap is 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 extra days. Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

questions.name: If the meeting is held on Monday, Kavya will attend it. Kavya did not attend the meeting. Which conclusion follows?

options.nameText: The meeting was not held on Monday

options.nameText:

 Monday

questions.solution: This is modus tollens: from “If P then Q” and “not Q”, infer “not P”. P = meeting on Monday, Q = Kavya attends. She did not attend, so the meeting was not on Monday.

questions.nameText:

 O, U, ?
questions.solution: Letter positions: C=3, F=6, J=10, O=15, U=21. The gaps are +3, +4, +5, +6. The next gap is +7, so 21+7 = 28. Wrapping the alphabet (28−26 = 2) gives B.

questions.name: A man walks 10 km west, turns left and walks 8 km, then turns left again and walks 10 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.nameText:
A man walks 10 km west, turns left and walks
 8 km, then turns left again and walks 10 km. How far and in which
 direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Path: 10 km West, then left (South) 8 km, then left (East) 10 km. The eastward 10 km cancels the westward 10 km, leaving him 8 km due South of the start.

questions.name: If FRUIT is written as HTWKV (each letter shifted two places forward), how is APPLE written in the same code?
questions.nameText:
If FRUIT is written as HTWKV (each letter
 shifted two places forward), how is APPLE written in the same
 code?
questions.solution: Shift every letter +2 in the alphabet: A→C, P→R, P→R, L→N, E→G. The code is CRRNG.

questions.name: In a class of 50 students, Amit is 12th from the top. There are 8 students between Amit and Riya, and Riya’s rank from the top is better than Amit’s. What is Riya’s rank from the top?
questions.nameText:
In a class of 50 students, Amit is 12th from
 the top. There are 8 students between Amit and Riya, and Riya’s
 rank from the top is better than Amit’s. What is Riya’s
 rank from the top?
questions.solution: Better rank means a smaller position number. Riya’s rank = Amit’s rank − (students between them) − 1 = 12 − 8 − 1 = 3.

questions.name: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. A sits second to the left of C. B sits at one extreme end. D sits between B and A. E does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits at the extreme right?
questions.nameText:
Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row
 facing north. A sits second to the left of C. B sits at one
 extreme end. D sits between B and A. E does not sit at an extreme
 end. Who sits at the extreme right?
questions.solution: B occupies the left end (position 1). D between B and A forces B, D, A. A second to the left of C places C at position 5. E takes position 4. Arrangement: B D A E C. Extreme right is C.

questions.name: Pointing to a photograph of a girl, Rohan said, “She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.” How is the girl related to Rohan?
questions.nameText:
Pointing to a photograph of a girl, Rohan
 said, “She is the daughter of the only son of my
 grandfather.” How is the girl related to Rohan?
questions.solution: The only son of Rohan’s grandfather is Rohan’s father. The daughter of Rohan’s father is Rohan’s sister.

questions.nameText:
A train 180 m long is running at 54 km/h.
 How long will it take to pass a pole?
questions.solution: Speed = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Time to pass a pole = length / speed = 180 / 15 = 12 seconds.

questions.name: If a:b = 3:4 and b:c = 5:6, find a:b:c.
questions.nameText: If a:b = 3:4 and b:c = 5:6, find a:b:c.
questions.solution: Make b the same in both ratios. LCM of 4 and 5 is 20. Scale a:b = 3:4 by 5 → 15:20. Scale b:c = 5:6 by 4 → 20:24. Combined ratio a:b:c = 15:20:24.

questions.name: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 18 and 252 respectively. If one number is 36, find the other number.
questions.nameText:
The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 18 and
 252 respectively. If one number is 36, find the other number.
questions.solution: Product of the two numbers = HCF × LCM = 18 × 252 = 4536. Other number = 4536 / 36 = 126.

questions.name: Find the remainder when 3^25 is divided by 5.
questions.nameText:
Find the remainder when 3^25 is divided by
 5.
questions.solution: Powers of 3 modulo 5 cycle every 4: 3, 4, 2, 1. Since 25 = 4×6 + 1, the remainder is the 1st residue in the cycle, which is 3.

questions.name: A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above the cost price and then gives a discount of 10%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.nameText:
A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above the
 cost price and then gives a discount of 10%. Find his profit
 percentage.
questions.solution: Take CP = 100. Marked price = 125. After 10% discount, SP = 125 × 0.90 = 112.5. Profit = 12.5%.

questions.name: A can finish a work in 15 days and B can finish the same work in 10 days. In how many days will they finish the work if they work together?
questions.nameText:
A can finish a work in 15 days and B can
 finish the same work in 10 days. In how many days will they finish
 the work if they work together?
questions.solution: A’s 1-day work = 1/15, B’s 1-day work = 1/10. Together = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6. So they finish the work in 6 days.

A number is first increased by 20% and then
 decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.solution: Net multiplying factor = 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96. This is a 4% decrease from the original value.

questions.name: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and the breadth is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage change in its area?
questions.nameText:
The length of a rectangle is increased by
 20% and the breadth is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage
 change in its area?
questions.solution: New area factor = 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08. The area increases by 8%.

questions.name: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
questions.nameText:
Two fair dice are thrown together. What is
 the probability of getting a sum of 7?
questions.solution: Favourable outcomes: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) — 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.name:
Passage

Remote work, once treated as an emergency arrangement, has become a lasting feature of the information-technology industry. Firms discovered that many roles can be performed without a shared office, and employees valued the time saved on commuting. Productivity studies, however, present a mixed picture. Individual task completion often improves when people work from home, but collaboration on complex problems tends to slow down. New joiners, in particular, learn less quickly when they cannot observe experienced colleagues. Companies have therefore shifted toward hybrid models: a few fixed office days for teamwork, with the remaining days left flexible. The success of such models depends less on software tools than on clear norms—when to meet, how to document decisions, and how to include people who are not in the room.

What is the main idea of the passage?

questions.name: Importance of Skill Development for Career Growth
questions.nameText: Importance of Skill Development for Career Growth
questions.solution:
Skill development plays an important role in building a successful career. In today’s changing job market, academic qualifications provide a foundation, but practical and professional skills help individuals perform effectively in the workplace.

Students can develop skills through online courses, internships, projects, workshops, and regular practice. Technical skills such as programming, data analysis, and digital tools are useful in many industries. At the same time, communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and time management are important for professional growth.

Skill development also helps individuals adapt to changes in technology and workplace requirements. Instead of depending only on theoretical knowledge, students can improve their employability by gaining practical experience and continuously learning new concepts.

However, skill development requires consistency and patience. Choosing relevant skills and practicing them regularly can produce better results than trying to learn everything at once.

In conclusion, skill development is an ongoing process. A combination of academic knowledge, practical experience, technical abilities, and soft skills can help students become more confident and prepared for future career opportunities.
